proof_rule: superset_proven requires an exhaustive DSH source-family inventory, native Julia implementations with executable differential evidence for every material family, no outstanding unverified families or runtime delegation, and passing required regression, lint, quality and CI checks. Reference-only cases never count.
assessment: A red-green-refactor cycle now targets native post-tool completion decisions against the exact pinned DSH policy stage. This remains an isolated projection: complete tool pipeline ordering and full result presentation are not proven. Native Julia indexed session search, persistent parent-child session identities, a framework-neutral session API, and an optional token-authenticated HTTP frontend are implemented independently. Indexed text behavior is checked against DSH; SDK directory/validation and Web authentication/HTML capability have bounded behavioral projections. DSH-native protocol shape, complete UI, session lineage and other feature families remain unverified; no overall feature-superset claim. Opt-in native JSON tool argument validation is differentially compared on bounded fixtures; complete tool-executor parity remains unverified. Optional Julia-native successful tool-output schema checks reject invalid results without exposing their value; 31 schema-level differentials against pinned DSH cover supported JSON values, but DSH's canonical output rendering and complete tool pipeline remain unverified. Native Julia tool batching now supports ordered result correlation, explicit concurrency-safe tool declarations, exclusive barriers, bounded dispatch, and drained cancellation. A deterministic pinned-DSH scheduler differential covers a narrow externally observable projection only; complete approval session/UI routing, policy-stage ordering, complete tool-result presentation, deferred contexts, and durable event logs remain gaps. Julia-native tool guards can request one-call approval through scoped, replaceable Julia event services; missing channels and non-grants fail closed. Nine isolated approval-resolution projections are compared against the pinned upstream implementation, but complete pre/post policy and UI consent flows remain unverified. A pinned upstream tool-body differential now checks that mid-execution cancellation suppresses an otherwise successful native Julia tool value; this is a bounded body-lifecycle projection, not complete post-execute policy parity. Opt-in Julia tool output renderers now preserve validated typed values while independently producing model-facing text; 15 pinned-DSH registry/renderer projections cover bounded text and schema behavior. This does not establish parity with DSH's final content blocks, UI presenters, post-policy stages, or deferred contexts.

oracle.implementation: Original pinned TypeScript source, transformed with Node built-in TypeScript support; no handwritten substitute oracle.
oracle.source_scope: Whole imported source files are hash-checked. Pure exported functions are extracted unchanged from those checked files.
oracle.dependency_resolution: The tool-registry dependency on HarnessError is resolved to its original defining error.ts module, without loading unrelated model runtime code.

limits: JSON-safe entry lists and valid patch field shapes only; YAML parsing, JavaScript expression interpolation and live loader updates are not exercised.
Bundle/package discovery, YAML parsing, profile installation, hot reload and npm resolution are unverified.

compares: fragmentation at every UTF-8 byte boundary of the chosen frame
limits: Representative newline JSON-RPC frames; no proof of all stream errors, maximum sizes, cancellation races, scheduling interleavings or network transport behavior.

compares: remote error code message and data
limits: Generated request ids are normalized to a fixed token; this tests correlation and payloads, not UUID identity. Timeout and cancellation diagnostics are not asserted equivalent.

compares: activation ordering on valid dependency graphs
asynchronous setup and effect cleanup settle before publication and teardown complete
explicit resource disposal unlinks owner registrations while the owner remains live, with idempotent disposal and reverse shutdown cleanup
limits: Shared lifecycle traces only. Native profiles preflight missing or cyclic dependencies; Cordis reactive pending, suspension and automatic reactivation are not implemented or claimed equivalent.
No equivalence claim for asynchronous generator plugins, configuration schema validation, intercepts or all isolation modes.

Live registration counts compare original Fiber.getEffects() with native ownership slots after fixture operations; these are dynamic disposal observations, not source declaration counts or a complete heap-leak proof.

compares: failed write settles only its request
later request succeeds on same peer
limits: A deterministic writer fails before emitting bytes. Partial writes, asynchronous stream error events and blocked-write cancellation are unverified.

compares: late event routing after scope disposal
completed outer waterfall task preserves downstream continuation and its resources until the longer callback finishes
limits: Test callbacks settle synchronously; arbitrary asynchronous listener interleavings, aggregate error details and in-flight teardown races are unverified.
Scope fixtures nest both ownership and routing. Cordis permits additional arrangements where those relationships differ.

The asynchronous waterfall lifetime case compares native deferred scope cleanup with an explicitly retained Cordis root disposed after all observed consumer Promises finish; it does not claim Cordis automatically retains roots during every dispatch.

compares: root-to-leaf, plugin-owned monotonic tool guards evaluated before body dispatch, including inherited scope denials, exact-disposer removal, and local tool shadowing
limits: Registry and selected-definition dispatch only; the reference invokes the actual selected definition execute callback directly. DSH executor admission, approval, guard, schema validation, output rendering, timeouts and parallel batches are not exercised.
Generic native ToolSpec does not impose DSH reserved names or mandatory output schemas. Invalid-registration comparisons cover acceptance, not language-specific exception messages.

Guard scenarios compare the pinned ToolsService.checkGuards() evaluation and selected-definition execution projection against native guarded invocation; DSH approval policy, full pipeline scheduling, and arbitrary concurrent disposal are not established.

compares: one service replaced while sibling service remains available
whole plugin generation staging and publication
failed staged initialization cleans effects and retains current composition
retained session invokes plugin-owned tool and event callbacks after profile replacement until its original generation is released
service binding retains its old plugin generation until a returned asynchronous callback task settles
limits: Whole-plugin staging is compared to explicitly separate Cordis contexts; this does not assert equivalence with reactive replacement of one fiber in one shared Cordis tree.

Per-service native bindings are compared to an explicit Cordis isolated service context. Retained native sessions and asynchronous service operations are compared to independently retained Cordis roots that dispose after their consumers finish. Concurrent activation races and arbitrary plugin side effects are outside these scenarios.

compares: notification callback closes its own transport and owned process
pending request rejects on callback close
callback returns and process terminates without a reader-supervisor wait cycle
notification callback awaits a request serviced by the same transport before closing
limits: The child producer and reference client both execute the actual pinned transport. Fixture application handlers emit a requested notification or answer a follow-up request. This isolates transport lifetime and reentrancy; it is not a DSH model or SDK application scenario.
Bounded completion detects this specific notification-reader cycle, not all callback and shutdown interleavings.

compares: native named-profile JSON persistence and activation preserve the selected plugins and configuration projected by upstream composition
limits: Only the common observable projection of plugin identity, order, and whole plugin configuration replacement is compared; DSH bundle discovery, patch grammar, hot reload, service bindings, and native plugin lifecycle require separate evidence.

Saved-profile format, filesystem semantics and name resolution are native Julia design choices, not claimed to match DSH persistence implementation; reference covers the shared composition projection only.

compares: literal, case-insensitive and whitespace-flexible search over conversation text
literal handling of regex metacharacters and Unicode case folding
role predicates, multi-session ordering, bounded search and live snapshots
revision-invalidated native trigram index returns exact case-insensitive, substring, whitespace and role-filtered results in deterministic stored-session order
indexed refresh after two successive atomic session updates compared against pinned upstream text selection
limits: The reference receives simple semantic text documents; Julia searches user/assistant message text. Full DSH event extraction, index-backed ranking, lineage, other event types and complete session-query service parity are unverified.
Only the eleven pinned differential fixtures are checked.
Index is an independent Julia implementation: current store writes invalidate it, while external file modifications require explicit refresh_index!; no DSH indexing algorithm equivalence is claimed.

compares: schema-enforced object, array, scalar, enum, const and exact-one union argument admission
path-qualified missing, type, closed-object and union diagnostics on pinned JSON fixtures
native ToolExecutor blocks rejected arguments before a user callback and exposes the underlying schema
limits: Only 31 JSON-compatible fixtures against the original pinned validator; unsupported-schema diagnostics, unbounded nesting, non-JSON objects, batch execution and every other DSH tool-executor behavior remain unverified.

Argument validation is opt-in via CheckedJSONSchema; existing opaque ToolSpec input schemas remain caller-defined. Separately checked outputs have only bounded schema-level evidence; approval, scheduling, cancellation, and complete tool-result rendering/presentation remain unverified.

compares: opt-in Julia tool-output admission after callbacks, against the pinned upstream JSON Schema validator
object, array, scalar, enum, const and exact-one union validation with result-relative diagnostics
valid results preserve their value, invalid outputs cannot escape through ExecutionResult.value, and output schema stays separate from model-visible input schema
limits: 31 bounded JSON-compatible cases against original DSH schema validation, not the complete DSH output rendering or presentation pipeline.
Julia output checks are optional and replaceable through tool_output_violations multiple dispatch; approval, batching, cancellation, and tool-output presentation parity remain unverified.

compares: Registered DSH tool bodies keep typed canonical return values distinct from output.render text blocks; Julia's optional render_output preserves the same distinction.
Passing output schemas admit readable model text, including empty text, Unicode, multiline values and numeric values; invalid canonical output does not reach the renderer.
Renderer invocation counts, preserved JSON-compatible values and rendered model-visible text for deterministic, independently authored fixture renderers.
limits: 15 bounded DSH registry/API and JSON Schema projections, not the full upstream ToolExecutionPipeline or final content-block snapshot semantics.
Julia currently exposes a single text projection rather than multimodal output blocks, presentation metadata, replayable UI views, post-execute waterfall hooks or deferred contexts.

compares: Exclusive barriers and bounded opt-in parallel dispatch
Per-call failures for unavailable or guard-denied tools
limits: The test invokes the unchanged pinned DSH scheduling function with an injected deterministic pipeline. The unexercised model-message factory is omitted only in this no-log test loader; no DSH runtime is loaded in production.

This is a bounded behavioral projection. Approval/policy preparation timing, complete tool result rendering, deferrable context, durable DSH session logging, argument parsing and cancellation races are not proven equivalent.

compares: Successful native tool returns retain their original values
Cancellation before dispatch does not execute a tool body
Cancellation during synchronous and suspended bodies drains execution and discards successful values
limits: The test invokes the original pinned DSH dispatchToolBody with a deterministic injected tool and minimal success projection; it does not exercise surrounding event, approval, post-execute, or durable logging services.
Only five bounded cancellation cases are compared; errors, nested cancellation, competing abort sources, and arbitrary timing remain unverified.

compares: One-call approval grant, explicit rejection, cancellation and unavailable-channel outcomes
Fail-closed missing-channel behavior with and without an explicit reason
Awaited Julia approval callback, listener withdrawal and no reuse of a prior grant
limits: The test invokes the exact pinned DSH approval-resolution method with an isolated service stub, not the entire DSH execution pipeline.

Julia uses scoped tool-approval events instead of DSH agent/UI services. Agent identity, audit logging, prompt presentation, policy interleaving and all end-to-end consent interactions remain unverified.

compares: Successful results accepted unchanged or with rewritten presentation text
Failed guards and failed callback results stay failures unless explicitly blocked
limits: The oracle invokes the original hash-pinned DSH post-execute method in isolation with fixed success and failure results, not a complete upstream agent or policy pipeline.
Deferred contexts, value replacements, rich multimodal output rendering, finalization, audit events and full cross-stage ordering remain unverified.

runtime_evidence.scope: Test-only DSH protocol clients exercise the framework-neutral JSON-RPC transport and process lifecycle against a pinned upstream CLI. A separate native Julia SessionStore comparison verifies persisted session history and workspace against actual upstream restart/resume observations. DSH SDK and Web behavior is delegated inside tests only; this does not establish native SDK, Web, or application feature parity.
guards: The CLI must be built at apps/cli/lib/bin.js in an unmodified tracked source checkout at the pinned revision; the same-version published npm package is not accepted.
Both SDK profiles must initialize, reject an uninitialized prompt, and validate session/query input. Unknown-method failures do not count as query support.
All five shipped profiles must appear in the configuration comparison.

The Web process must become ready, exchange its own launch token for a browser cookie, serve authenticated HTML with status 200, and serve a nonempty built static asset. Matching startup failures cannot pass.

Successful-turn scenarios use the pinned upstream llm-mock-server on IPv4 loopback with four scripted success requests. The pinned SDK must produce the exact fixture response and its resumed model request must contain the original user prompt, assistant response, and continuation prompt.

scenarios.projection: Thirteen request outcomes per profile: prompt before initialization, initialization, directory get/set/get, idle wait, empty and blank query validation, missing directory and unchanged directory, absent-session resume, unknown method, and shutdown; ordered notification method/session/type trace; process exit.

Independent native Julia Session workspace against actual pinned DSH SDK observations: initial directory, relative navigation, rejection of nonexistent directories, preserved directory after failure, relative path resolution, and nested Julia include resolution from the observed workspace. DSH does not execute Julia source; the include projection is a native Julia capability checked against DSH's reported directory.
Complete --dump-config stdout, stderr, and exit status through the test-only DSH frontend adapter with native process launcher.

Loopback server startup on an OS-selected port; seven unauthenticated/method/path responses; token-cookie redirect metadata; authenticated HTML and public SVG body lengths and SHA256 digests, content types, cache headers and ETags; conditional asset request; owned process shutdown and exit signal.

Actual upstream HarnessClient versus Julia helpers: successful prompt, wait, exact final response and finish reason; a fresh process resumes the persisted session despite a different initialization directory, then completes another turn. Compare ordered notification projections and complete model-request messages, model/output-cap/stream options, local server outcomes, and the restored user/assistant history.

Native Julia plugin-provided SessionStore persists user and assistant messages, then resumes in a fresh session with the original working directory and prior history; the resulting continuation-history projection is compared against the pinned upstream SDK's actual resumed provider request. Julia does not invoke DSH for production persistence.

Native Julia SessionAPI open, workspace read/change, invalid path, empty-query rejection, missing resume, unknown method and saved identity retention are compared with pinned DSH SDK outcome categories; different Julia-native method names and envelopes are intentional.

Optional native Julia HTTP server provides token-authenticated HTML and a session RPC route. Shared upstream Web authentication and HTML success properties are compared, not frontend bytes, assets, or protocol parity.

normalization: SDK session events retain method, sessionId and event type, excluding event bodies containing generated identifiers or timestamps.
Configuration output replaces each isolated DSH_HOME with <home> and normalizes CRLF.
Authenticated Web HTML replaces the isolated home and ephemeral listener origin before comparing its complete byte length and SHA256 digest.
Each Web launch token and signed cookie is used only against its own isolated process; their random values and expiry times are excluded from comparison.

Successful prompt receipts compare the presence of a nonempty message identifier, excluding its generated value. Provider-request message payloads retain all blocks and content, replacing only the time-context plugin's sampled timestamp and elapsed-time values. Provider credentials, generated HTTP metadata, and system-prompt metadata are outside that comparison.
unverified: External model responses, generated tool execution, approval and question interaction flows, other persistence histories and recovery/migration cases, jobs, goals, schedules, MCP and third-party package replacement behavior are not exercised by these runtime scenarios.
Browser JavaScript interaction, WebSocket behavior, desktop behavior, TLS, remote deployments and ACP protocol conversations remain outside these comparisons.

Native session working-directory comparisons cover directory state, path resolution and built-in Julia include resolution, not arbitrary filesystem operations, third-party tool filesystem behavior or full native SDK functionality.

No native DSH SDK/application/Web implementation is supplied by the test-only DSH protocol adapters. Their successful forwarding and server startup are reference-only and do not establish product parity.

Native session snapshots persist message roles, text and kinds plus working directory, not arbitrary message metadata, token accounting, in-flight operations, tool resources, or the complete DSH on-disk session format.

Native SessionAPI supports independent Julia JSON-RPC sessions but has not been shown to implement every DSH SDK operation or wire shape; HTTP.jl extension serves a minimal native page and JSON-RPC endpoint rather than the full DSH Web application.

interpretation.required-differential-cases: The suite requires these comparisons on every run; current pass or fail is determined by execution, not by this metadata.
interpretation.unverified: No behavioral parity for the complete family has been established.
interpretation.unverified-remainder: The explicitly listed projections have differential cases; all other behavior in the family remains unverified.
interpretation.reference-support: Upstream test helpers or support code, not an automatically verified user capability.
interpretation.native-implementation-unverified: The family needs independent Julia implementation and relevant differential evidence; some native subset may exist, but a DSH runtime proxy cannot count as parity.
interpretation.reference-support-only: Test-only utilities compared to DSH source to keep the oracle and transport fixtures stable; not a JuliaForever2 product capability.

limits: Valid consumed event shapes; upstream envelope validation, malformed block fields and all event semantics are outside this comparison.
The compared DSH-specific helper now exists in differential test support only, not the JuliaForever2 production API; these comparisons provide no native feature-parity evidence.
Explicit executable mode only; installed-package discovery, source-loader discovery and SDK timeout defaults are unverified.
Only caller-selected environment variables are compared. SDK options.env replaces its environment; native DSHProfile.environment adds overrides to the inherited environment.
The executable name is normalized to a fixed node token. Profile launch is not proof of every feature within the selected profile.
The compared DSH-specific helper now exists in differential test support only, not the JuliaForever2 production API; these comparisons provide no native feature-parity evidence.
